Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Samir (Infra SE) vs Mark (CTO), Lena (ML Eng), Daniel (Platform), Sofia (Security), Tom (SRE)

[00:00] Alex: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'll let priya and samir intro but high level we want to walk through per-model tuning notes - llama, mistral, qwen - and talk through rope scaling, moe routing costs, and the kv caching/batching knobs. sound good?
[00:12] Mark: yep, that's perfect - we want actionable guidance, we have a low-latency product path and curious about on-prem vs dedicated.
[00:18] Priya: cool thanks mark. quick intros - priya shah, solutions eng at redwood, i focus on runtime perf and quantization. samir handles on-prem infra.
[00:28] Samir: hi all.
[00:30] Lena: thanks. we run a streaming summarization pipeline - target p95 latency < 250ms for 1-2k token sequences. currently evaluating Llama 70B and Mistral base-class, also prototyping Qwen.
[00:45] Daniel: and we have strict data residency - likely want VPC or on-prem.
[00:50] Priya: noted. quick agenda: 1) per-model behaviors (rope scaling etc), 2) MoE routing and cost/latency tradeoffs, 3) batching and kv cache patterns, 4) quantization guidance, 5) deployment constraints. we'll surface numbers from our internal benchmarks and then agree next steps.

[01:08] Priya: starting with ROPE - short version: different models implement rotary embeddings / rope with different implicit scale factors and training recipes. Llama's rope tends to be more stable across lengths but still suffers from extrapolation drift as sequence length increases; Mistral and Qwen have different decay characteristics.
[01:25] Lena: can you clarify what you mean by decay characteristics? like it loses positional signal after X tokens?
[01:30] Priya: yeah, exactly - you see drift where older positions' relative signals attenuate, which affects long-context QA and summarization. we recommend rope scaling strategies: either linear interpolation of frequencies (rescale during compile) or train-time interpolation if you can finetune. in serving, we provide an option to rescale rope at runtime - it's a compile-time kernel + small inference overhead but often worthwhile for 2-3x longer contexts.
[01:55] Alex: quick note - for Llama 70B we saw ~10-15% perplexity improvement on long-context eval when applying runtime rope rescaling, and latency hit was ~3-5% depending on kernel selection.

[02:12] Mark: is that supported in hosted or only in dedicated/private?
[02:15] Priya: supported across all modes but on shared hosted we may route to a compatible variant; for Dedicated/Private you can pin a build with rope-rescale enabled.

[02:25] Priya: moving to MoE - main tradeoff: gating adds compute per token for expert selection and increases memory footprint. Qwen-MoE style models often route top-2 experts which boosts quality but doubles some attention/ffn compute depending on implementation. the routing cost is small for batch sizes > 8 due to amortization but significant for low-latency single-stream inference.
[02:50] Samir: to add, MoE routing also complicates KV cache layout - you may need per-expert kv shards which increases cache misses if routing is dynamic. that leads to jitter in latency.
[03:05] Daniel: so for our p95 <250ms usecase with single requests, MoE might be risky?
[03:10] Priya: yes, it's a risk. options: 1) use dense model variant (Mistral/dense Qwen) for latency path, 2) force deterministic gating or reduce top-k gating to 1 to lower overhead, 3) run MoE on Dedicated with pre-warmed experts and batching. we can share config examples; i'll include gating knobs in the spreadsheet.

[03:35] [03:36] Alex: reference - we attached a benchmark spreadsheet in chat (link shared later).

[03:40] Priya: on KV cache - important distinction between prefix caching (store full key/values for previously seen prefix) vs token-level KV caching. prefix caching gives best repeated-context perf but uses more memory. for Llama-style models, KV cache hit-rate is high for streaming summarization so enabling automatic prefix caching reduces token work by ~30-60% depending on prompt reuse.
[04:05] Lena: we often have user-provided system prompts + 1-2 turns of context, seems like that should be high hit-rate. what's the memory tradeoff?
[04:12] Priya: for 70B Llama, KV for 2k tokens is roughly X GB per replica - (note: approximate) - 2k tokens ~ 16-20GB of kv in fp16, quantized kv can drop this. with our quantized KV paths (4-bit per-key compression in the runtime) we see ~35-40% memory reduction with small perf hit.
[04:35] Samir: caveat on on-prem: with HBM-limited GPUs you may prefer to offload cold KV shards to host memory or use NVMe rolling cache. that adds latency. we can size GPUs accordingly.

[04:55] Priya: batching strategies - continuous batching vs fixed-window batching. continuous batching (adaptive) gives best throughput and keeps latency bounded for moderate concurrency; but at very low qps with tight p95 you want single-request optimizations + microbatching of size 1. Redwood runtime supports both and we expose batcher policy. we recommend latency SLOs drive policy: p95 <250ms -> batcher policy low latency with max batch size 4, flush timeout 5-10ms. throughput optimized -> larger batches and longer flush.

[05:30] Mark: any heuristics for batch size vs GPU type?
[05:33] Priya: yes - A100 80GB can sustain larger batches for 70B models; for Mistral smaller model you can keep batch sizes higher to amortize kernel overhead. we'll provide a matrix in the spreadsheet.

[05:45] Priya: quantization notes - 4-bit (QLoRA style / GPTQ) often gives best cost/perf for dense models with minimal accuracy loss on classification/summary tasks, but for some generation-sensitive tasks you might see artefacts. Mistral tends to be more robust to 4-bit than Llama in our tests; Qwen's numeric stability depends on tokenizer alignment. per-model recommended profiles: Llama-70B -> 8-bit or 4-bit with calibration and KV compression, Mistral-34B -> 4-bit aggressive, Qwen-43B -> 4-bit with extra outlier detection.

[06:20] Lena: do you do PTQ vs GPTQ???
[06:22] Priya: we support multiple pipelines; GPTQ-style per-tensor quant with fine calibration worked best for our benchmarks. note that quantizing KV arrays is trickier - we've implemented quantized-kv kernels that trade slight accuracy for memory win.

[06:35] Sofia (security): quick question - when you say KV offload or NVMe caching, how is data encrypted at rest and keys managed?
[06:41] Samir: good Q - on VPC and Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. NVMe volumes are encrypted using customer-managed keys (via KMS) and audit logs capture access. we'll include SOC2/ISO notes in the security doc.

[06:55] Priya: also for on-prem we can integrate with HSM for key wrapping; our runtime supports explicit key injection and we don't persist unencrypted prompts. we'll send the checklist.

[07:05] Alex: circling back to MoE routing cost numbers - quick example from our internal bench: Qwen-MoE style (top-2) running single-stream on a 8xA100 80GB cluster had median latency 220ms but p95 jitter to 420ms due to routing-induced cache misses; dense equivalent gives 190ms p95 with much lower jitter.

[07:28] Mark: those jitters are a concern. are there mitigations besides densifying model?

[07:32] Priya: yes: pre-warm expert shards, prefer routing determinism, pin requests to specific replicas to stabilize caches, and use dedicated capacity so experts stay resident. each mitigation reduces flexibility but helps latency. we'll show config examples.

[07:50] Daniel: asked: how do rope rescale and quantization interplay? any gotchas?
[07:55] Priya: good question - rope rescale changes attention kernel math and can amplify quantization noise if you do aggressive 4-bit. we recommend applying rope rescale in fp16 kernels where possible, and only quantize the final runtime path after testing. also avoid doing both rope-rescale + aggressive per-tensor quant without calibration.

[08:20] Alex: quick demo snippet: (Alex shares screen briefly) the spreadsheet has run configs: model, seq len, batch size, quant profile, rope-rescale enabled/disabled, observed median/p95. i'll highlight: Llama-70B seq=1024 batch=1 fp16 median 120ms p95 210ms; Llama-70B 4-bit quant median 95ms p95 190ms; Mistral-34B 4-bit median 45ms p95 80ms. these are indicative.

[08:52] Lena: great - can you add our target tokenization and prompt shapes so results map to our workload?
[08:56] Alex: yes please upload sample prompts, we'll re-run bench.

[09:01] Priya: deployment notes - VPC/private differences: hosted shared will offer fastest time-to-value but you can't access HSM directly; Dedicated gives predictable capacity and we can enable KMS integration; Private/on-prem gives full control but we need more planning for NVMe/HBM sizing and network fabric. for on-prem we typically recommend Mellanox/infini-band for large clusters for MoE workloads.

[09:28] Tom (SRE): re: network - we have standard 100g infra, is that sufficient?
[09:31] Samir: 100g is okay for smaller clusters; MoE at scale with frequent expert shuffles benefits from 200g or RDMA for best p95.

[09:40] Mark: any motor points for procurement? like committed capacity vs burst?

[09:44] Alex: yes - if you need low p95 and MoE stability, reserved Dedicated is the safe path; for experiments hosted or burst on Dedicated is ok. procurement should factor in sustained hours vs burst. we'll send a pricing sketch.

[09:58] Priya: closing - immediate actions: we will run the notebook with your sample prompts and return a tailored benchmark; share VPC/on-prem checklist and security docs; provide gating and rope-rescale config examples.

[10:12] Mark: perfect, thanks all.
[10:15] Alex: thanks everyone - we will follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the on-prem planning session.

[10:20] (meeting ends)
